title: Republic of Botswana: World Bank Group Country Climate and Development Report
temporal_coverage: Country climate-development diagnostic published in 2025; combines historical observations and referenced studies with current-risk overlays and scenarios extending to 2050.

title: National Drought Plan: Republic of Botswana
organization: Republic of Botswana, prepared by Nnyaladzi Batisani under the UNCCD Drought Initiative
temporal_coverage: Historical droughts through the 2020 plan; includes a 2015 vulnerability assessment, RCP4.5/8.5 projections and proposed 2020-2023 actions.
methodology: National drought-risk synthesis and proposed sectoral governance actions.
limitations: Uses a 2015 risk assessment; recommendations are not evaluated implementation or current status.

title: Makgadikgadi Framework Management Plan 2010, Volume 2, Chapter 5: Wildlife Resources and Human Wildlife Conflict
organization: Department of Environmental Affairs, Government of Botswana, with the Centre for Applied Research
temporal_coverage: Assesses historical and current-at-the-time wildlife and human-wildlife conflict patterns, with focus groups in April-May 2010.
methodology: Combines DWNP Problem Animal Control records, multi-year aerial counts, spatial mapping and 18-22-person focus groups in four villages.
limitations: The report warns aerial counts vary in coverage and may substantially undercount; focus-group findings are historical and site-specific.

title: Human-wildlife conflict a growing challenge
organization: Botswana Daily News / Botswana Press Agency, reporting an Acting Director of the Department of Wildlife and National Parks briefing
temporal_coverage: Reports a February 2025 briefing, including national wildlife-conflict figures for 2022-2024.
methodology: Government newspaper account of an Acting DWNP Director's Ntlo ya Dikgosi briefing; incident figures are attributed to the speaker.
limitations: Not an independent incident dataset; the account provides national statements without named hotspots.

title: Gender and Equity Considerations for Building Climate Resilience: Lessons from Rural and Periurban Botswana
organization: Kutlwano Makwatse, Leatile Modie, Morati Mpalo and Caitlin Blaser Mapitsa; Sustainability (MDPI)
temporal_coverage: Household baseline research in Xhumaga and Ramotswa, reported in 2022; exact fieldwork dates are not stated.
methodology: Participant-coded household narratives and survey with 141 residents in Xhumaga and Ramotswa, followed by community feedback meetings.
limitations: Quasi-random qualitative sample, not statistically representative; fieldwork dates are unstated and participant data are restricted on ethical grounds.
